lifecycle.description: Observed work lifecycle state. lifecycle_transition_target.description: Agent-requestable lifecycle transition targets. failure_attribution.description: The failed attempt's terminal failure attribution exactly as the event-based reader resolves it. Absent on every attempt whose state is not failed.

source_event_id.description: The durable failure, rejection, or correction-request event that opened this correction; its diagnosis and strategy are that event's directions.

then.description: CD-0210: an active or completed outside-repair disposition grants no managed pin authority. else.description: CD-0210: an ordinary or resumed pin runs the managed instance read, so the workflow identity stays strict and the registry-verified definition identity — version, digest, and the declared obligation set — is required in full.

cancelled_instance_closes.description: All-time count of work items in this item's primary Project that have lifecycle completed while their workflow instance is cancelled (the CD-0183 D4 repair route).

workflow_definition_version.description: Version of the pinned workflow definition the registry verified for this pin.

workflow_definition_digest.description: Registry digest of the pinned workflow definition; verifies through the builtin registry.

obligations.description: Sorted exact evidence obligation IDs the pinned definition declares across root, step, and rigor declarations; the same collector admission reads.

outstanding_evidence_kinds.description: Sorted unique outstanding evidence kinds from the pin's transaction snapshot, including recovery check verification. outside_repair_route.description: The declared outside-repair reconciliation operation, with completed and resume modes (CD-0210).

relation_query_label.description: Labels the relation read surface serves. Derived from contracts/relation-vocabulary.v1.json: every kind's forward label, plus each declared inverse label.

subject_ref.description: The author's claim about what the finding concerns; never dispatch-owned subject identity. Bounds: 1..128 code points inclusive

domain_id.description: A current Domain of the Product registry, validated against the registry and the approved affected scope at admission. Bounds: 1..256 code points inclusive

product_wide_rationale.description: Required exactly when domain_id names the registry's root Domain; a child Domain never carries one. Bounds: <=512 code points inclusive

finding_id.description: Core-derived from the source event sequence and ordinal; never authored.

kind.description: The generic claim vocabulary of an authored finding. A ranked oracle finding projects the empty kind: its identity is the oracle tie, never a generic claim class.

evidence_refs.description: The evidence that supports the finding. A ranked finding without an oracle tie projects null; the core reader owns that wire shape.

status.description: A finding is a reported claim, never acceptance. The open status names a ranked review finding the lineage currently holds open: still a claim, and open.

source_kind.description: Present only on a ranked review finding: the entry carries an oracle tie and rides the open-set lineage, never the generic worker-claim notebook.

oracle.description: The typed oracle tie of a ranked review finding: classification plus the owner, predicate/law, case, and control references that bind it.

source_event_frontier.description: The work item's maximum event sequence at read time, so a packet built from this view can be compared against current state before spawn.

oracle_receipts.description: The prior typed control-execution receipts this work retained, in log order: reported regression baselines with their exact identities, never current-subject acceptance.

subject_commit.description: The sole core-derived current subject, as a raw commit OID. Native receipt subject_ref remains commit:OID and the store normalizes that reference once.

oracle_preparations.description: Only native preparation records selected by the immutable job's readiness refs. No raw output or alternative readiness authority.

research_findings.description: The selected research entries the latest declaration anchor resolved, in authored order, beside the generic findings under the shared 32-finding bound. Omitted when the declaration selects nothing.

work_context_unavailable.description: The shared work-context view exceeded its bound. The work pin and continuity remain readable, but packet construction refuses this marker.

worker_oracle_mechanism.description: The source-level owner of one obligation: the Project that owns the repository, one contained source path, and the symbol or entry point that owns the behavior. A directory name alone does not identify a mechanism.

path.description: A normalized relative repository-contained source path. Bounds: 1..512 code points inclusive

worker_oracle_law_binding.description: One pinned law revision that explains an owner's obligation, plus the clause or criterion it serves.

domain_id.description: An approved affected Domain of the active parent contract, validated against the current Product registry at admission. Bounds: 1..256 code points inclusive

obligation.description: The bounded invariant statement this owner owes. Bounds: 1..512 code points inclusive

predicate_ids.description: The parent-approved predicates this owner covers. Bounds: 1..8 items inclusive

case_id.description: A stable case: identity, unique within this work item. Bounds: 6..128 code points inclusive

expected_state.description: A bounded description of the expected state, never a new predicate DSL. Bounds: 1..512 code points inclusive

control_id.description: A stable control: identity, unique within this work item. Bounds: 9..128 code points inclusive

predicate_ids.description: The parent-approved predicates this control exercises. Bounds: 1..8 items inclusive

recipe_source.description: The exact pinned recipe manifest, not the candidate's modified harness. Native preparation resolves its file bytes, cwd, build-selected witnesses, and environment without test execution. Dispatch consumes that qualified preparation, never an automatic compiler or control run.

argv.description: The exact argument vector, never shell text. Bounds: 1..32 items inclusive

cwd.description: A contained relative working directory. Bounds: 1..512 code points inclusive

expected_result.description: The declared exit-status result the harness must produce. Slice A admits pass (exit 0) only.

required_evidence_role.description: The evidence role the control's receipt must carry.

readiness_evidence_refs.description: The qualified native preparation run references for this exact owner/case/control bundle, parent contract, Project, raw subject, and environment. A legacy green command, unrelated evidence binding, compilation assertion, or zero-selector control is not readiness. Bounds: 1..8 items inclusive

worker_acceptance_oracle.description: The owner-level acceptance oracle: typed immutable worker-job content. Owners with obligations, a finite case inventory, and executable controls with exact evidence requirements. The store validates the closed graph and its authority joins; the serialized oracle content is bounded by the store at 32 KiB and refused whole on overflow, never truncated.

worker_job_direct_caller_allowance.description: The conditional direct-caller scope an editing job may carry (CD-0227 D1): the permitted Project, the changed owner mechanisms, and the parent contract's approved Domain and pinned law boundaries. It authorizes only the minimum source and test changes that preserve an existing direct caller's approved request behavior.

project_id.description: The permitted Project. It must equal the recorded job's project_scope. Bounds: 2..128 code points inclusive

mechanisms.description: The changed owner mechanisms the caller repair preserves, reusing the oracle's mechanism shape. Bounds: 1..8 items inclusive

domain_ids.description: The approved affected Domains of the active parent contract the allowance keeps, joined like the oracle joins Domains. Bounds: 1..8 items inclusive

law_bindings.description: The pinned law revisions the allowance keeps, joined like the oracle joins law. Bounds: 0..8 items inclusive

workflow_step.description: The instance's current step; null when the work item holds no workflow instance (imported work).

pending_project_handoff.description: The work's newest unconsumed Project-session handoff (CD-0182 amendment): the bounded repository job a receiving session must consume through project_handoff_consume before managed execution. Absent when no handoff stands unconsumed on the work.

ready_worker_jobs.description: CD-0205: the work's dispatch-ready worker-job revisions in the exact inputs.worker_job packet shape, so a dispatcher selects one by job_id and binds its recorded content verbatim. Readiness is the one predicate dispatch admission applies. On a size-capable pin a job carries the caller_exclusions its implementation dispatch binds (CD-0227 D1); a dispatcher drops them for every other lane. Absent when no revision is ready.

checks_repair_review_jobs.description: CD-0205 D4: exact satisfied repairing revisions awaiting their one confirming review. These are not ordinary ready jobs. Only review lanes may bind them; core dispatch admission still enforces the repairing acceptance, single-use review authority and retry wall.

active_verify_leases.description: CD-0096 D5: the reading session's held verify leases, newest first, bounded. Absent when the session named no identity or holds none.

workflow_instance.description: Typed workflow-instance absence. Present only when the work item holds no workflow instance; the packet fabricates no step for it, and a launch never creates one.

work_context.description: The available work-context view. An evaluated over-bound view emits work_context_unavailable instead. An evaluated absent context emits neither member.

observations_read.description: The paged read of the whole observation population, newest first. The observations field holds only the newest window that fits the envelope.

continuity_projection_page.description: CD-0016 as amended: the closed lossless transport for one oversized continuity projection. The identity header repeats exact scalar work, step, instance, and watermark identities only. One page never carries complete authority: a consumer joins every page of one projection digest before it uses the projection, and reconstruction precedes use.

work_version.description: The exact work-item version the captured projection was derived from, when the capture exposes it; absent otherwise.

workflow_instance.description: Typed workflow-instance presence, exactly the store's captured marker: "present" when the work item holds a workflow instance, "absent" when it holds none (imported work).

workflow_step.description: The instance's current step; null when the work item holds no workflow instance (imported work).

watermark.description: The exact source watermark of the captured projection.

projection_page.description: The exact byte page of one canonical continuity JSON document. encoding is fixed; digest is the SHA-256 of the complete canonical document; total_bytes is the document's exact UTF-8 byte length; offset is this fragment's starting byte; data carries the exact UTF-8 fragment text. data is not independently parseable JSON and is not a summary: a fragment cannot carry complete authority. Concatenate the decoded fragment strings by byte offset, check total length and digest, then parse the reconstructed document exactly once; reconstruction precedes use, and no consumer inspects partial contract, question, intent, or context data.

data.description: The exact UTF-8 fragment text of the canonical document at offset. Each page carries at least one whole code point and fills the real remaining envelope capacity; no fixed fragment cap bounds it.

next_kind.description: The continuation the authenticated envelope next_cursor resumes: "projection" continues this document's next page, "boundaries" resumes the original boundary-page continuation, null ends the read.

continuity_read_result.description: The concord_work_trace.continuity result: the complete typed inline snapshot when the measured final envelope fits the unchanged 51,200-byte limit, or the closed lossless projection-page transport when the fixed projection does not fit. The root property list only names the keys the two closed branches own; each branch carries the full constraints and exactly one branch must match. A page cannot carry complete authority; a consumer joins the page sequence and reconstructs the document before use.

continuity_boot_projection_reference.description: CD-0090 D6: the deterministic boot projection reference for an oversized continuity projection. It carries the exact small identity header, the complete captured boot projection's digest and byte length, and the canonical initial continuity read pointer. It is not the projection and cannot carry complete authority: reconstruction through the referenced authenticated pages precedes use, and a later read may describe newer state or a different session's held leases than this captured snapshot.

work_version.description: The exact work-item version the captured projection was derived from, when the capture exposes it; absent otherwise.

workflow_instance.description: Typed workflow-instance presence, exactly the store's captured marker: "present" when the work item holds a workflow instance, "absent" when it holds none (imported work).

workflow_step.description: The instance's current step; null when the work item holds no workflow instance (imported work).

watermark.description: The exact source watermark of the captured projection.

projection_omitted.description: Exact omitted-projection status: the boot packet carries no projection body and no fragment, and claims no complete contract, question, intent set, or evidence.

read_pointer.description: The canonical initial concord_work_trace.continuity read that starts a separate authenticated projection stream for this projection. The captured boot digest describes the boot snapshot; it is not a promise that later read bytes match.

limit.description: The continuity read's default boundary window.

verdict.description: CD-0023: recorded acceptance verdict. Absent with a redaction omission when the reader is the recorded executing actor.

depth.description: Hops from the requested work item. An edge at depth 1 is stored. An edge at a greater depth is derived by same-kind closure, which only a transitive kind admits.

source_watermarks.description: CD-0200: one freshness verdict per registered knowledge source in a Product-wide answer, home first. Absent from a single-source answer.

work_size_inputs.description: What this change will touch, for the work-item size model (CD-0229 D4). Name the files, a behavior phrase, or both. The tool derives kind, stage, audience, Domains, packages, and repositories; the model decides the size. There is no size field: a proposed size is refused.

paths.description: Repository-relative files or directories the change will edit. Bounds: <=64 items inclusive

behavior.description: A phrase for the behavior the change will alter, when the files are not known yet. Bounds: 1..256 code points inclusive

security.description: True when the change touches authentication, authorization, secrets, or data safety.

user_visible.description: True when the change removes or reverses behavior users see, or changes UI or UX.

blast_radius.description: The widest thing a defect could break: one function, one package, several packages, or a public surface (CLI, tool, schema, wire format).

estimated_production_lines.description: Production lines you expect to add or change, tests excluded; a relative-size estimate, not a delivered-code measurement or assignment cap. Bounds: 1..100000 value inclusive

work_size_summary.description: The work item's current effective size, model decision, optional operator override, model version, and recording time. Absent when work has never been sized.

defect_intake.description: Capture admission record (defect intake). Required for kind bug, optional for kind research, refused for every other kind; the core enforces the kind rules and the admission decision.

operator_size.description: The operator's size for the work item (CD-0229 D6). It needs a consumed operator approval; reason explains the override. The effective size changes in place on the same work item.

size_inputs.description: Reruns the model on fresh declared inputs; reason explains why. The core re-derives every other input and updates the size in place without a successor.

worker_failure_attempt_identity.description: The core-derived identity of one authorized worker attempt: the registered lane, the positive attempt epoch, and the packet digest the dispatch authorization recorded, plus exactly one of the explicit no_job marker or the recorded job revision. A missing subject is legal: a pre-launch attempt has no child session or subject.

worker_failure_attribution.description: The typed failure_attribution block. The recorded origin carries the producer observation and the core-derived identity; the explicit legacy_unavailable marker marks explicit historical absence and carries neither.

worker_failure_attribution_read.description: One failed attempt's resolved terminal failure attribution: the terminal event identity, the source payload version the log recorded, and the decoded block. The attribution is null when a capable terminal recorded none; a source version below the boundary resolves the explicit legacy_unavailable marker. The 8192-byte whole-block bound is the store's own bound, never a schema keyword.

tag.description: The typed host observation tag: a terminal error, a held retry, a bare cancellation, or the coordinator's abandonment request the host adapter observed. A cancellation and an abandonment carry no error identity; an abandonment is admitted only on the abandoned terminal and keeps cause and basis unknown.

event_type.description: The host event type that carried the observation, at most 256 UTF-8 bytes. Bounds: 1..256 code points inclusive; <=256 UTF-8 bytes inclusive

session_id.description: Bounds: <=256 code points inclusive; <=256 UTF-8 bytes inclusive

message_id.description: Bounds: <=256 code points inclusive; <=256 UTF-8 bytes inclusive

error_name.description: Bounds: <=256 code points inclusive; <=256 UTF-8 bytes inclusive

error_code.description: Bounds: <=256 code points inclusive; <=256 UTF-8 bytes inclusive

status_code.description: The HTTP-shaped status the host supplied, absent when the host supplied none. Bounds: 100..599 value inclusive

worker_failure_host_observation.description: The typed host observation one host_event source carries: which host event was seen, for which session and message, and the typed terminal error fields when the host supplied them.

worker_failure_identity.description: The closed attempt/integration union of core-derived identity. Exactly one variant is present and it matches kind; the producer never authors it.

worker_failure_integration_identity.description: The core-derived identity of a combined integration run: the native run that failed, and either the exact accepted input population in event order or the explicit inputs_unavailable marker for a lease recorded before its event watermark — never both, and the marker never stands for an empty accepted population.

worker_failure_job_binding.description: One recorded worker-job revision reference: the job identity, the revision, and the content digest. That the revision is exactly the one the dispatch recorded is a store join, never a schema check.

observer.description: The boundary that observed the failure. The authenticated route sets the observer tag; it is never an authority string a worker supplies.

phase.description: The closed phase the failure was observed in. Only the boundary that observed a phase may emit it.

cause.description: The causal classification the observer claims. Typed observations classify only what their boundary owns; failed tests and missing reports never automatically mean an implementation defect.

basis.description: What the causal claim rests on. A hypothesis stays labeled even with citations; a supported claim names admissible immutable evidence.

sources.description: The observed structured diagnostic, in the order the boundary observed it. An absent or empty array is not the observation shape. Bounds: 1..8 items inclusive

diagnosis.description: The bounded causal diagnosis, distinct from the exact observation. At most 1024 UTF-8 bytes. Bounds: <=1024 code points inclusive; <=1024 UTF-8 bytes inclusive

worker_failure_observation.description: the direct producer observation a coordinator correction action may carry as its optional failure_attribution input. Closed over observer, phase, cause, basis, sources, and diagnosis exactly: the recorded block's origin, core-derived identity, input population, sequence, and commit members are core-derived and are never authorable here.

kind.description: The closed variant of the observed diagnostic: a host terminal/error observation, admitted failed-report evidence, a validator error with location, an existing result or review finding reference, or a native run.

locator.description: The immutable locator of the observed record. Store the fields actually supplied; never an invented locator. Bounds: <=512 code points inclusive; <=512 UTF-8 bytes inclusive

digest.description: One sha256:<64 hex> content digest of the observed record, where one is available. Bounds: 71..71 code points inclusive; 71..71 UTF-8 bytes inclusive

message.description: The exact observed message the boundary supplied, at most 2048 UTF-8 bytes. Bounds: <=2048 code points inclusive; <=2048 UTF-8 bytes inclusive

worker_failure_source.description: One entry of the observed structured diagnostic: the closed variant tag, the immutable locator of the observed record, the content digest where one is available, and the exact observed message where the boundary supplied one. A host_event source carries the typed host observation and no other kind may.

worker_failure_subject.description: A typed immutable reference to an existing recorded subject: the terminal event that carries the core-observed delivery, or the retained native run. The store joins resolve the reference; nothing here copies a commit.

packet_schema_version.description: The retained packet schema identity the original dispatch recorded: the adapter selects the historical reader by this pair, never by today's current revision.
